subject: Stakeholder mapping & champion enablement — FinovateBank
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finovatebank.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Stakeholder map (as discussed):
   - Economic buyer: Tom Reynolds (VP, Digital Channels) — responsible for budget sign-off.
   - Procurement lead: Elena Park (procurement@finovatebank.com) — procurement/CLM timeline.
   - Security/legal: Sofia Alvarez (information security contact) — SOC2 / data residency questions.
   - Day-to-day champion: Rajesh Menon (product) — will drive PoC and internal adoption.

2) Decision criteria you called out: latency under 300ms P95, private deployment option (VPC), predictable per-token economics, and SOC2 evidence.

3) Proposed next steps:
   - Marissa will share a short champion enablement pack (talk tracks + ROI bullets) for Rajesh by early next week.
   - Marissa/Neha to share SOC2 summary + deployment options.
   - Marcus to coordinate a procurement timeline call and get procurement contact.

Attachments: Finovate_MA_plan_v1.pdf (draft mutual action plan) — Marcus attaching the initial plan.

Can you confirm the stakeholder roles above and a good time for a 30-min enablement call for Rajesh (we can do 20–30 mins)?

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finovatebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Thanks Marcus — that lines up well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Economic buyer: confirmed Tom Reynolds. He wants a high-level TCO estimate + risk mitigation plan before a formal business case.
- Procurement: Elena Park will own contracting. She usually needs a procurement questionnaire + a list of relevant security artifacts.
- Security: I'm the day-to-day security contact — we'll need SOC2 type II summary, data residency commitments (US-East preferred), and clarifications on KMS/HSM support.
- Champion: Rajesh is absolutely our internal champion and can run the PoC — he'd like a concise enablement pack to help him brief stakeholders.

Can you send a SOC2 summary and a short deck for Rajesh? For timeline, procurement will likely take 4–6 weeks once we put a SOW in.

Also, Tom asked for a ballpark run-rate estimate for a Dedicated instance plus an option for hosted API for lower-risk workloads — nothing detailed, just a range.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Information Security | FinovateBank
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finovatebank.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Appreciate the confirmations, Sofia — tagging Neha (SE) and Lauren (AM) to help close any technical and procurement gaps. Attached two short files: SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf (one-pager) and Finovate_MA_plan_v1.pdf (draft mutual action plan).

Three things from my side to enable Rajesh and the team:

1) Champion enablement pack (attached / inline bullets):
   - Elevator pitch (20s): Redwood Inference is a production-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) so you can run LLM features at scale without building the stack.
   - Top 3 ROI points Rajesh can use: (a) reduced per-token cost via batching & caching compared to ad-hoc infra; (b) faster time-to-market via our hosted API and turnkey dedicated capacity; (c) reduced ops burden — we manage kernel selection, autoscaling, and fallbacks.
   - Suggested internal ask: 30-min final stakeholder briefing (tech + procurement) led by Rajesh with Redwood support.

2) Security/compliance notes:
   - SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf summarizes scope and controls.
   - KMS: we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers; HSM integrations available for Dedicated/Private.
   - Data residency: we can guarantee region pins for Dedicated/Private (US-East available).

3) Ballpark pricing:
   - Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit): ~$40k–$85k/month depending on GPU class and commit level (rough range).
   - Hosted API (metered): $0.03–0.10 per 1k tokens depending on model family and throughput.

Next steps I propose:
   - Rajesh enablement session next Wed or Thu (we're flexible) — 20–30 mins.
   - Marcus will follow up with procurement cadence and DocuSign draft for SOW (we can prefill to speed Elena's review).

Links: HubSpot deal and DocuSign draft above.

Let me know best times for Rajesh and procurement. Happy to join the enablement call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Development Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finovatebank.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Quick technical notes to support procurement/security review: 

- Deployment options:
  • Hosted API: fastest onboarding, multi-tenant, best for early testing.
  • Dedicated: reserved GPU pool in US-East, customer isolation, can bring your own keys to KMS.
  • Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads where data cannot leave customer network.

- Security artifacts available: SOC2 Type II summary (attached by Marissa), penetration test summary (available on request), and encryption-in-transit & at-rest docs.

- Integration notes for Rajesh: we provide SDKs (Python/Node), sample PoC repo, and a 2-week PoC playbook that outlines test prompts, traffic patterns, and acceptance criteria.

I can join Rajesh's enablement session and the procurement call if useful — proposed 30-min slots Thu 04/15 10:00am or Fri 04/16 2:00pm ET.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finovatebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Thanks Marissa / team — that was very helpful. 

Rajesh is available for an enablement session on Thu 04/15 at 10:00am ET (please send a calendar invite). Elena (procurement) will join the procurement timing call next week — I'll introduce Marcus and Elena over email after the enablement.

Action items from our side: I'll confirm whether Tom wants a separate executive summary for the business case.

Please send the SOC2 summary and the one-page mutual action plan so Rajesh can circulate internally.

Regards,
Sofia
Director, Information Security | FinovateBank
